sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Domung [dev]; contains no Yout Wam phonological data. Included only because it is the nearest-relative phonology held by the project and confirms that no Yout Wam description exists in the SIL-PNG literature it cites.

sources.citation: Moe, Jonathan A. 2023. A Phonology of the Domung [dev] Language of Papua New Guinea with Acoustic Analysis. MA thesis, Trinity Western University. vii+119 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Domung, not Yout Wam. Mentions Yout Wam only as a neighbouring Yupna language in which Gabutamon Domung speakers are bilingual (pp. 3-5, citing Gray 2007: 47), and lists the phonological descriptions that exist for Finisterre languages (Table 4, p. 13: Yupna sub-group covered only by Spaulding 1988/1992/1994 Nankina and Reed 1993/2000 Yopno; none for Yout Wam). Reports Claassen & McElhanon 1970: 66 on stress being 'probably non-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat' (p. 11).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Yout Wam (yout1234) and family nodes Yupna (yupn1242) and Bwana-Moam-Tapen (bwan1242); ISO 639-3 code page for ytw; Wikipedia 'Yout Wam language' and 'Finisterre languages'; ELAR deposit 0344 (Slotta 2014, Documenting Yopno Diversity, languages bop, dev, yut)
sources.note: No additional references for Yout Wam anywhere: Glottolog cites only Gray 2007; the ELAR Yupna-valley deposit covers Yopno, Bonkiman and Domung, not Yout Wam; API searches for "Yout Wam" in OpenAlex (0 hits), CrossRef (no relevant hits), Semantic Scholar (0), Google Books API (0), archive.org advanced search (0) and TransNewGuinea.org (no language entry) returned nothing.

sources.citation: [extra, already held by the project] Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. Canberra: ANU. https://doi.org/10.15144/PL-A23.45
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the Finisterre Stock generally and names Rawa, Yupna (Yopno) and Wantoat; Yout Wam is not identified as a language in 1970 and no Yout Wam data underlie the statement. Catalog has no record for yout1234, so there is nothing to agree or disagree with; at most this is weak family-level evidence that stress in Yupna-family languages was thought to be non-contrastive.

sources.note: Nothing on phonology or stress. Says Yout Wam is spoken only in Yout village, shares 38-45% lexical similarity with four Domung villages (Gabutamon 45%, Bobongat 42%, Kian 39%, Ayengket 38%), and its only source is Gray 2007 (a manuscript survey) under 'knowledge through personal communication'; 'not a major language with a body of literature and research'.

sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A23.45
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level survey; Yout Wam is not distinguished (Yout village falls under 'The Domung language.. about 850 people.. near Tapen', p. 54). One sentence on stress for the whole Finisterre stock, p. 66 (PDF p. 22): 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat. In none of these languages does it carry a heavy functional load.' 'Yupna' here is the language sketched in 6.1.5 (Kewieng/upper Yupna valley), not Yout Wam; no statement of stress placement.
